+++
kind = "proof"
of = "det-tf-cone-zero-sections"
uses = ["det-tf-cone-leg-lifts", "pur9-def-normal-cone"]
+++
The zero section of a normal cone is defined by the positive-degree ideal of its graded
algebra, and that ideal is generated by the degree-one part.

*(1)* Since $J$ is generated by $c_1^\cdot I$, the images under the first leg of the
degree-one elements $I/I^2$ generate $J/J^2$ as an $\mathcal O_E$-module, hence generate the
positive-degree ideal of $\operatorname{gr}_J\mathcal O_C$. The quotient of
$\operatorname{gr}_J\mathcal O_C$ by the pulled-back zero-section ideal is therefore its
degree-zero part $\mathcal O_C/J=\mathcal O_E$.

*(2)* The pulled-back ideal is generated by the classes in $J/J^2$ of the elements of
$L=c_2^\cdot I\,\mathcal O_C$. A product of $n$ such classes is the class in $J^n/J^{n+1}$ of
an element of $L^n$, and $L^n\subset J^{n+1}$ makes it zero. So the pulled-back ideal is
nilpotent, its vanishing set is all of $N_EC$, and the reduction of $N_EC$ maps into the
zero section.
